#228313. “A Southern Storybook Brought to Life.” Inside South Carolina’s Luxurious Lowcountry 20,000-Acre Montage Palmetto Bluff.

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1519 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Outsideonline ↗ Open Full Page

“A Southern Storybook Brought to Life.” Inside South Carolina’s Luxurious Lowcountry 20,000-Acre Montage Palmetto Bluff.

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1519 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Outsideonline

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • (Photo: Top Left: Rebecca Norris; Bottom Left: Andrew Baldino; Right: Montage Palmetto Bluff).
  • Ever come across an incredible hotel that stops you mid-scroll and makes you think: Wow, wouldn’t it be something to stay there?
  • I’m traveling down a very narrow two-way road in a tinted Chevrolet Suburban when the chauffeur stops abruptly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

(Photo: Top Left: Rebecca Norris; Bottom Left: Andrew Baldino; Right: Montage Palmetto Bluff).

Ever come across an incredible hotel that stops you mid-scroll and makes you think: Wow, wouldn’t it be something to stay there? We do, too—all the time. Welcome to Friday Fantasy, where we highlight amazing hotels, lodges, cabins, tents, campsites, and other places perched in perfect outdoor settings. Read on for the intel you need to book an upcoming adventure here. Or at least dream about it.

I’m traveling down a very narrow two-way road in a tinted Chevrolet Suburban when the chauffeur stops abruptly. He points out two alligators sunbathing on the rocks in the May River on our right. That is my first sighting of an alligator or any reptile in over 15 years—except for a strangely cute banana boa constrictor in my high school science class. I’m no fan of them.

That gator pair, and a few more, dot the river, alongside the long road leading up to Montage Palmetto Bluff, a five-star resort in South Carolina’s Lowcountry.

The sandy dirt road, shadowed by live oak trees draped in Spanish moss—a signature of the Lowcountry landscape—eventually opens onto the resort’s central property: a sprawling white mansion called the Main Inn.

After the driver helps unload my bags from the truck, resort staff greet me and lead me inside across the wide porch, a hallmark of any traditional Southern residence. The dark wooden floors creak under my feet, the same kind of creaking that reminds me of walking into the comfort of my grandma’s house.

Industry observers note that montage Palmetto Bluff is a 20,000-acre property tucked between Hilton Head Island and Savannah, Georgia. It has over 200 guest rooms, suites, cottages, and other residences, called Village Homes, Moreland Village Homes, and Signature Residences. (I stayed in one of the signature residences.).

The property also offers ample outdoor and wellness activities, including a shooting club, golf course, a 13,000-square-foot spa, a lawn and racquet club, and over 20 miles of walking and biking trails.

For folks who want to throw a lavish, intimate event or wedding, Palmetto Bluff features two beautiful chapels: the May River Chapel and the Somerset Chapel. The latter is where Justin Bieber and Hailey Baldwin held their wedding ceremony in 2019. Through the church’s arched windows, you’ll get magnificent views of the sunset.

In a recent development, the resort is approximately a 30-minute boat ride from Daufuskie Island, a remote, bridge-free barrier island between Hilton Head Island and Savannah, Georgia. It has white-sand beaches, one paved road on the less-developed side of the island, and a rich Gullah Geechee culture. The Gullah Geechee people are descendants of enslaved West Africans who were forced to work on plantations along the southeastern coast of the United States.

In a recent development, despite the resort’s beauty, it sits atop a dark history. In the Antebellum Era, Palmetto Bluff was home to several plantations where enslaved people grew lucrative crops, including indigo, cotton, rice, corn, beans, and sweet potatoes.

“We believe it is key first and foremost to acknowledge the suffering endured by the enslaved individuals who lived and labored on this land,” Meghan Lamb, senior manager of marketing and public relations at Montage Palmetto Bluff, tells me. “These stories deserve to be shared openly and thoughtfully, both to honor those who came before us and to ensure their experiences, contributions, and enduring legacy are never forgotten,” she adds.

Lamb, who walked my fellow housemates and me through much of the property and, while sharing the Bluff’s rich history, also had an excellent eye for spotting gators.

As a Black person whose ancestors were enslaved on southern plantations, hearing about the history here was a painful reminder, but a lack of acknowledgment would have been even more so.

During the Civil War, Union troops captured the land, and many white families and enslaved people fled the area. Wealthy bankers and businesspeople later purchased the property, and the land changed hands several times. A banker named Richard T. Wilson bought the property in 1901, expanded it, had a large mansion built on the grounds, and gave the estate its current name: “Palmetto Bluff.” The mansion burned to the ground in a 1926 fire; the ruins remain preserved on the grounds today.

Palmetto Bluff is now owned by a private equity firm that specializes in resort management, Henderson Park and South Street Partners.

I stayed in one of the signature residences, houses available for rent for a period of time, with three others for four days and three nights.

The Signature Five Bedroom Lagoon Residence 1003 is a mansion with high ceilings and luxurious bathrooms, plus a fireplace, a porch, a separate cottage, and a large communal dining table nestled in the center of the home.

Recent findings suggest that I chose the bedroom in the back left corner of the house; it had warm, yellow lighting, deep mahogany-colored walls, a king-sized bed, a lush en-suite bathroom, and some of the softest sheets I’ve laid my head on. Despite a packed schedule, I rested easy each night.

You can view room rates and book your stay at a signature residence here.

On my first night, we were welcomed with a Southern-style buffet in our signature residence. The menu was astounding: a traditional Lowcountry boil with shrimp, corn, potatoes, and sausage, plus fluffy biscuits, mac and cheese, collard greens, and peach cobbler for dessert.

There are also several places to dine across the property. Guests can indulge in fine Southern cuisine at the Octagon or at the elegant River House, which is where I ordered my first Wagyu steak. Brunch is served at Buffalos, and premium cocktails are available at Hush, a speakeasy. Along the lagoon waterway that runs through the resort is Fore & Aft, which serves delicious Mexican fare. Flame is a 1950s-vintage pizza truck you can easily walk up to and grab a slice in the evenings, Wednesday through Sunday. Buzz is a cozy cafe (I got a toasty ham-and-cheese croissant one morning that didn’t disappoint), and Melt is the Bluff’s ice cream parlor. The property even has its own gas station with a small grocery store.

In a recent development, for a fun treat, you can make your own s’mores at the massive fire pit behind the Main Inn every night at 9 P.M. I did, and it brought me back to when I used to make them as a kid by the campfire in my parents’ backyard.

As I mentioned—my schedule was packed, but I managed to fit in a few outdoor activities. The 20-plus miles of trails on Palmetto Bluff offer scenic walking and e-biking tours.

I had never been on an e-bike before, so I was pumped for this chance to do so on some beautiful trails. I liked that I could switch between regular biking and an electric boost to reach nearly 20 miles per hour. The combination of speed, wind in my hair, and stunning trail views was exhilarating, so much so that I even made the very risky decision to FaceTime my girlfriend with one hand to show her how much fun I was having.

Andrew Baldino, the public relations and marketing coordinator at Montage Palmetto Bluff, led the e-biking tour and pointed out spots most people tend to miss. One of those, he noted, is River Road. The appeal? Sweeping live oaks, long Spanish moss, and extensive lush greenery, he tells me.

The Golden Hour E-Bike Excursion lasts for one hour and 15 minutes and costs $90 per person. You can book your slot here.

According to recent reports, on the second day of my stay, I took a paint-and-sip class at my signature residence with renowned artist Amiri Farris, known for incorporating Gullah Geechee imagery into his work. We painted a blue crab because they’re often found in South Carolina estuaries, tidal creeks, salt marshes, and rivers.

On the third day, I embarked on the Daufuskie Island History Excursion tour. Because the tour lasts about four hours, you’ll need to book it early in the morning. My tour started at 7:30 A.M. It was one of the highlights of my trip. I saw dolphins along the way and learned about the island’s rich history on a golf-cart tour of the island’s untouched parts after hopping off the boat. Our captain, who steered the boat and led the golf-cart tour, made the experience even more worthwhile as he’s developed deep relationships with people on the island and shared stories about the island’s characters, bringing a humorous, jovial vibe to the trip.

Industry observers note that private tours for up to six people cost $895, tours for up to 12 people cost $1,195, and tours for up to 16 people cost $1,295. You can book them here.

I left my trip feeling nourished, calm, and more knowledgeable about the Lowcountry than before I arrived.

Lamb put it beautifully when I asked what about the Bluff makes visitors want to return—and even buy property on the resort: “It’s a Southern storybook brought to life.”.

#228310. The Six Formative Moments in Every Climbing Career

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1265 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Climbing ↗ Open Full Page

The Six Formative Moments in Every Climbing Career

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1265 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Climbing

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Placing your first cam is a memorable, and often horrifying, moment in every climber's career.
  • Every climber has experienced a truly unforgettable moment.
  • In a recent development, not all climbers will share these exact memories, but there are some key moments that define almost every climbing career.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Placing your first cam is a memorable, and often horrifying, moment in every climber's career. (Photo: Andrew Burr).

Every climber has experienced a truly unforgettable moment. For some, it’s tagging that tree after climbing the Nose. For others, it’s the vast bulk of Denali filling the windshield of the de Havilland Otter. For yet others still, it’s that first splitter at Indian Creek, that first wide crack at Vedauwoo, or that first roof at the Shawangunks.

In a recent development, not all climbers will share these exact memories, but there are some key moments that define almost every climbing career. Whether you’re a climber from Southern California or from Northern Vietnam, these will probably be familiar, and they probably changed the way you do business. They’re rites of passage, and when newer climbers pass through those same gates, you’ll grin knowingly, nod your head and say “Shit, we’ve all been there!”.

Recent findings suggest that these days, just about every climber gets started indoors, and the transition from gym to crag is a big deal. When you tentatively emerge from the womb of the climbing gym, the possibilities of ascending ACTUAL ROCKS are infinite and exhilarating. There you are with your laminated lead card still attached to your harness, squinting and blinking in the unfamiliar sunlight, craning your neck ever upward under a vast sea of stone….

On closer inspection, you see them—occasionally chalked, but devoid of color, tape, or any visual aid that would denote a route. This is concerning, and your consternation only deepens as you pull on. What follows is a desperate pumpfest during which you grasp ineffectively at every possible (and impossible) hold, ignore your footwork, and mutter phrases like “Is this one on?” and “5.9, my ass.”.

Now, I realize that several crusty veterans are about to flood the comments section with hardcore tales from the pre-gym era—how the closest they’ve ever come to touching plywood was hammering home-slung timber chocks into cracks, how much of the Earth’s granite was still cooling in subterranean caverns when they started climbing, how their favorite Triceratop died of exhaustion during a regular 16-day approach. Sure, not every climbing career began with a heady gym to crag transition, but the impertinent youths whose did would agree—we’ve all been there.

You’re inching left on a sketchy traverse when your belayer blasts you with an unsolicited beta spray.

“Watch that rope, dude. It’s behind your leg.”.

But you don’t got this, and when your foot pops and that tenuous crimp unlatches, you fall. The rope catches mid-calf and suddenly you’re upside-down and giving the wall the old “Glasgow Kiss”—a headbutt, in other words. Wear a helmet, kids. After righting yourself and lowering to the ground, it’s not entirely clear what hurts more: that throbbing, rope-shaped welt fused with tiny purple and yellow fibers or your pride.

Nope, it’s definitely your pride, but you can salve your damaged ego with the knowledge that almost every climber suffers the indignity of a super-ugly-upside-down-leg-behind-the-rope whipper at some point. Most will only suffer it once, because this hard-knock lesson improves rope management which makes for better, safer lead climbing. Don’t feel too bad, you’re not alone in making this rookie mistake. We’ve all been there.

It might happen on that 5.9 you’ve climbed more times than you’ve had hot dinners, or perhaps on the tail end of a 12-hour minor epic. Either way, as you prepare to lower or rappel, you notice that something is not quite right. Scratch that—it’s horrifically wrong. You’re not clipped in properly, and had you have weighted the system, you’d have taken the Significant Ride.

In the days and weeks following this potentially fatal near-miss, make a serious review of your systems. The experience should form a powerful lesson—almost as powerful as the gastro-intestinal evacuations that occurred after the bad taco you ate in El Potrero Chico.

Sources indicate that complacency and fatigue are often factors, but the true reason for serious human error is this: Your systems suck. Maybe you’re weren’t applying best practice, or maybe you’re not consistent enough with those that you do use. A smart (or sufficiently chastened) climber will embrace this opportunity to analyze, criticize, and ultimately improve techniques, because although we’ve all been there, it’s not somewhere we wish to return.

There comes a time in a climber’s life when they must place a piece of traditional protection, either by design or by default. Then comes a sudden realization, a piercing moment when it becomes clear that one’s entire being is committed to the inner workings of a spring-loaded camming device or the security of an asymmetrical hunk of aluminum. Eyes glaze over, total recall of high school physics occurs, Rainman-esque calculations of friction coefficients and force vectors take place….

Sources indicate that this moment is polarizing. It alternately fills climbers with invigoration, or with an existential dread so profound it would make Friedrich Nietzsche look like the Dalai Lama. Climbers then find themselves in one of two camps—either “newly minted trad climber” or “fuck that, never again.” And whichever camp you find yourself in, you’ll probably come to regard the other as having serious and incurable mental deficiencies. But no matter which side of the fence you end up on, we’ve all been there.

Recent findings suggest that what was that? Oh, nothing. Just your A2 pulley disintegrating, along with your dreams of onsighting The Widowmaker (VI 5.14a X A4 M10ish) at HardBastard Canyon this year. Worse still, it happened in the gym. Oh, the humanity.

Recent findings suggest that your first climbing injury comes with two realizations. The first is that your immediate future is going to look a lot different from how you envisaged it five minutes ago. The second is that you’re not invincible. Everybody thinks it can’t happen to them, until it does.

The recovery period for a finger injury is horrifically tedious—six ponderous months of pulling ever so gently on holds that are no smaller than the West Buttress of Denali. Afterward, you won’t be able to tear the skin off a custard, but you’ll be a gun at warming up, an ace at stretches, and an absolute legend at taking rest days. But here’s an idea… why not buck the trend and start doing these BEFORE you get injured? We’ve all been there, but if we can prevent it from happening, why do we all wait until it’s too late?

Belayers are a dime a dozen, but a real climbing partner is a true gift. But what makes a real partner?

Industry observers note that A real partner is just as stoked as you are, if not more so. They don’t say things like “why” and “how much.” They say things like “hell yes” and “let’s do this.” They can spoon you in a bivvy cave without it getting overly weird. They will empty your piss bottle on the understanding that you’ll return the favor sometime. They will lend you that No. 6 without a moment’s hesitation. They really, really want to see you crush that pitch.

Industry observers note that put simply, a real climbing partner is someone you would follow to the ends of the earth, and regularly do. A real climbing partner can turn a bad climb into a good one, a good climb into a great one, and a great climb into a life-changing experience. Forming deep and genuine connections is one of the finest aspects of the sport, and if there is one thing I truly hope, it’s that we’ve all been there.

This year, beat high lift ticket prices by volunteering as a patroller, adaptive ski instructor, or buy qualifying flight tickets to a number of select locations (Photo: South_agency/Getty Images).

With lift ticket prices regularly topping $250 across North American mountains, budget skiing takes strategy. Outside dug into this season’s best hacks for scoring free lift tickets for skiers and snowboarders, from airline promotions at nine marquee resorts, to volunteer opportunities, and even to going downhill with a U.S. Forest Service ranger.

This winter, we’re tracking the snowiest mountains in America and the rare super El Niño on the way. Now, here’s what you need to know for the 2026-27 winter season when it comes to snagging your free passes.

Located in the San Juan Mountains of Southwest Colorado, Purgatory Resort is a 30-minute drive from Durango. With over 1,600 acres and an average snowfall of 260 inches annually, the mountain offers a blend of steep tree skiing and open groomers.

During the 2026-27 season, Purgatory is offering skiers and snowboarders a free season pass in exchange for 14 days of volunteering. Four of those shifts must fall during peak season, including winter holidays, Presidents’ Day weekend, and spring break.

Several other mountains across the country offer similar incentives for those volunteering on the slopes. Winter Park Resort in Colorado, North Carolina’s Beech Mountain Resort, and Whiteface in Upcoming York all provide free lift tickets in exchange for volunteering on ski patrol or the safety team.

According to recent reports, alaska Airlines’ Atmos Rewards Alpine Getaways for the winter ski season lets passengers show a qualifying boarding pass at nine participating western U.S. and Canadian ski resorts for free lift tickets, rental upgrades, and resort discounts.

Eligible passengers flying into the following airports get a free full, same-day, or half-day ticket.

Jay Peak Resort in Vermont is celebrating its annual Day for the Devoted on November 27, 2026, featuring 750 free lift tickets.

In a recent development, “Day for the Devoted opens the season with a thank you to the people who make this place what it is, and an invitation to anyone ready to become a part of it,” the resort writes on its website. You can register for the event here.

According to recent reports, buying a qualifying Helly Hansen ski jacket or pair of pants gets you a free day or a buy-one-get-one ticket at participating resorts across North America and Europe. Clothing must be from the latest Helly Hansen ski collection.

Buy your gear, find the resort you’d like to ski, and submit your receipt to redeem a pass. More information is available on the company website here.

It has been revealed that adaptive skiing nonprofits rely on volunteers to help people with disabilities experience skiing. In many cases, volunteers receive a complimentary lift ticket for the day they’re helping.

At Eagle Mountain Therapeutic Recreation in Showdown, Montana, volunteers 16 and older can receive free passes and lunches on the days they work. Those who work four events can receive a day pass to be used at any time, while those who commit to eight or more days will receive a free pass for the season, according to the program website.

Sources indicate that the Outdoors for All at The Summit at Snoqualmie and Stevens Pass in Washington offers a variety of volunteer programs, from ski and snowboard instructors to support in snowshoeing and Nordic skiing. Full-time volunteers are eligible for a discounted season pass, while part-time volunteers receive a same-day lift ticket. All volunteers also receive ExpertVoice pro deals and have access to instructor development, adaptive teaching experience, and clinics.

Every Friday beginning January 30 through April 3, 2027, intermediate skiers and snowboarders can spend an hour skiing with a U.S. Forest Service (USFS) staff member through the Ski With a Ranger Tour. Attendance is first-come, first-served and limited to 12 participants daily.

It has been revealed that participants must provide their own lift ticket, but the program is part of a free conservation education initiative that shares the USFS mission in ski area management. Participants will also learn about natural resources and environmental stewardship, the USFS writes on its website.

According to recent reports, kelso Carapia, a recreation specialist with the USFS Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, has been leading the program for 14 years. She told Outside that participants can expect to learn about a host of topics, including water ecology, forest health, animals, survival strategies, fire management, general land stewardship, and the cultural and geological history of the Tahoe Basin.

Sources indicate that ski experience is necessary. The route is on intermediate and blue terrain only, and skiers will access at least two lifts as part of their tour.

In a recent development, “This is not a ski lesson,” Carapia said. “It is an interpretive tour. As much as we prioritize safety and comfort of our participants, we are not there to instruct.”.

Recent findings suggest that heavenly Mountain Resort straddles the California-Nevada border in South Lake Tahoe, California, and Stateline, Nevada. With 4,800 skiable acres across four base areas, it’s also a major winter destination.

Ski With A Ranger tours are led by the United States Department of Agriculture’s Forest Service Conservation Education staff and volunteers through a cooperative effort between the Forest Service and Heavenly Mountain Resort.

From an Editors’ Choice-winning tent to featherweight insulation, here’s what we found.

In a recent development, another Editors’ Choice winner, the Blaze 60 is a lightweight pack that carries better than it has any right to. “You never really feel the pounds, even with north of 40 on board,” our reviewer stated. A plastic framesheet, cushy padded hipbelt, and easy-to-adjust torso keep it feeling comfy under a load.

According to recent reports, A fixed-length trekking pole in 2026? If you’re not using your poles to support a tent, it could make sense. The Distance Carbon removes the weight and complexity of an adjustment lock—a common failure point of adjustable models—to create a rigid, reliable pole ready for long days in the mountains.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for a bag upgrade, the Spark—a 1 lb, 1.4 oz model that’s warm enough for almost any above-freezing adventure—is a safe bet. Stuffed with 850-fill down, the Spark disappears into a pack, and a draft tube and baffles along the zipper help seal out the chill when it’s in use.

“Luxury” is a word we wouldn’t often apply to our backcountry sleep systems, but this one earns it. The 3.5-inch-thick Tensor Trail is plush for a one-pound pad, and our testers reported that its consistent baffles were exceptionally comfortable; on a trip to Michigan’s Isle Royale, reviewer Stephanie Pearson reported she fell asleep before sunset and ended up sleeping in the next morning.

Originally designed with alpinists in mind, Mountain Hardwear’s Ghost Whisperer line is perfect for anyone who likes to move fast. The 800-fill down insulation is warmer than the piece’s 8.3-ounce weight would suggest. Bonus: When not needed, it packs into its own pocket for easy stowage.

Recent findings suggest that if the Ghost Whisperer’s selling point is its weight, the Helium’s is its durability. In our testing, the Helium survived crampon strikes and scrapes against rock and ice without visible harm. Nice touch: Fleece-lined hand pockets and deep internal pockets allow you to keep necessities close at hand.

An ultralight rain jacket is no good if it can’t, you know, keep out the rain. The Guardian Air delivers on both counts: At 7 ounces, it’s firmly on the featherweight side of the category, but its waterproofing is also head and shoulders above most competitors. In testing throughout Montana’s Bitterroot and Lolo National Forests, we found it shrugged off precip as well as far heavier models.

Radios make communication far easier during winter adventures, and we’ve yet to use a radio that we liked as much as the Rocky Talkie. With a range of up to 5 miles and a battery life of up to 5 days, its ready to go deep this winter.

The Tungsten UL 2 is a lightweight tent that doesn’t compromise: A freestanding design with dual doors and vestibules makes it simple to get in and out of and reliable in heavy weather, while pre-bent and color-coded clips make it easy to set up out of the box.

Industry observers note that the Scarpa Rapid Mid GTX is one of my personal favorite hiking boots on the market, pairing a light 10.6-ounce weight with a Vibram MegaGrip outsole that can handle everything from the Utah desert to Appalachian peaks without wavering. A sock-like design hugs the foot, providing stability even on tricky scrambles.

#228303. Latest Update: It's Time To Stop Saying These 6 Phrases To Your Grandkids. Here's Why.

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1374 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Huffpost ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: It's Time To Stop Saying These 6 Phrases To Your Grandkids. Here's Why.

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1374 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Huffpost

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As grandparents, you want all of your relatives to feel happy, loved and connected in your company.
  • Sometimes, unintentional or even well-meaning comments from grandma and grandpa can “create an environment where grandkids feel uncomfortable or insecure,” Ann-Louise Lockhart, a pediatric psychologist and president of A New Day Pediatric Psychology in San Antonio, told HuffPost.
  • That’s why it’s crucial to be more mindful about how we communicate with our grandkids not just during this time but all year round.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As grandparents, you want all of your relatives to feel happy, loved and connected in your company. Unfortunately, that doesn’t always happen.

Sometimes, unintentional or even well-meaning comments from grandma and grandpa can “create an environment where grandkids feel uncomfortable or insecure,” Ann-Louise Lockhart, a pediatric psychologist and president of A New Day Pediatric Psychology in San Antonio, told HuffPost.

That’s why it’s crucial to be more mindful about how we communicate with our grandkids not just during this time but all year round.

“It can be hard to change the way you say things but it’s crucial to be intentional with your words, and be aware of how much words can impact the way your grandkids think and feel about themselves and their relationship with you,” Lockhart said.

We asked Lockhart and other experts which common phrases are best avoided and what to say instead.

One note before we dive in though: If you’ve used any of the below phrases before — or happen to slip up in the future — try not to worry too much or beat yourself up over it.

“It’s never too late to start being more mindful of how you approach interactions with your grandchildren,” remarked Andrea Dorn, a psychotherapist and author of the “Mindful Steps” children’s book series.

“It undercuts parental authority, which can have long-standing consequences,” she remarked. “Furthermore, it models for kids that they might find themselves in situations where it’s in their ‘best interest’ not to tell their parents. This can be especially dangerous if a child is being groomed by a predator or feels bad about themselves for getting bullied.”.

Instead, you want to reinforce the importance of being honest with their parents — no matter what.

“Grandparents can find other ways of doting on their grandchildren without crossing the boundaries their parents have put in place,” Delawalla said.

Comments about a child’s body or weight are a “huge no,” Lockhart noted, as they can contribute to body image and self-esteem issues.

“As responsible adults, it’s our duty to support and encourage children to be confident in their own skin,” she stated. “Let’s avoid making any comments that could potentially harm their self-worth and lead to insecurity. I hear about it constantly in my practice from young children through adults. Harsh comments from grandparents like this are remembered and replayed over and over again.”.

Sources indicate that dorn also told HuffPost that any remarks or comparisons about physical appearance can be problematic. This includes things like: “Have you lost weight?” or “Wow, you’re so much taller than your brother now!”.

“The matter with comments about physical appearance or comparisons to others is that they place an increased focus on the importance of external features over internal traits,” she mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that instead, she suggested saying something like: “It’s wonderful to see you again! I’ve missed spending time with you. How have you been?” Open-ended questions about your grandkids’ current interests, activities or hobbies are great, too.

“Being genuinely interested in who kids are on the inside helps them to feel seen and heard, and sends the message that each person can be valued just as they are right now and that people are more than just how they look or what they wear,” Dorn remarked.

Any comments about your grandkids’ food intake — “You eat so fast,” “You’re a member of the clean plate club,” “Looks like you haven’t touched a thing on your plate” — are best kept to yourself.

Recent findings suggest that “Learning about food and hunger cues is an key developmental step in childhood,” Dorn said. “Comments about ‘good’ and ‘bad’ eating habits can influence children to adjust their eating behavior in reaction to another person’s comments or perspective, rather than following the signals their body is sending them. It may also trigger feelings of shame or confusion in the moment or over time.”.

Recent findings suggest that it’s really not necessary to comment on your grandkid’s plate or their eating habits. But if you’re going to say something, Dorn recommended focusing on the importance of listening to one’s body.

“You can also model this practice by listening to your own body, and stopping when you feel full and eating when you feel hungry,” she said. “Modeling good eating habits is more important than any comments we can make.”.

When you see your grandchild acting ungratefully while opening a mountain of presents or throwing a fit because they didn’t get their way, you might be inclined to make a comment about how spoiled they are.

If this kind of behavior is happening pretty consistently, it probably has less to do with the kid and more to do with the way they’ve been parented.

As Ryan Howes, a clinical psychologist from Pasadena, California, told HuffPost: “If they are acting entitled and ungrateful, this may be a behavior they learned or saw modeled for them, maybe even something that was reinforced by their parents. So giving them all the blame isn’t fair. Suck it up or talk with the parents, but keep the judgment to yourself.”.

As a grandparent, it’s natural to want to connect with your grandchildren in this way, especially when you’re so excited to see them. However, many kids may not feel comfortable giving hugs and kisses on demand, and it’s crucial for the adults in their lives to respect this.

Recent findings suggest that “While this phrase is likely filled with love and a completely normal desire to foster closeness and connection with a child, it can also unintentionally take away a child’s right to autonomy and pressure them to abandon and second-guess their body boundaries,” Dorn said. “This can send confusing messages about consent.”.

In order to respect your grandkids’ boundaries, you could instead phrase this as a question: “I’d love to give you a hug. Is that OK?”.

But if they say “no,” accept their answer and move on.

Recent findings suggest that “Make sure not to push further or use guilt with a comment like, ‘Please, just one? I’m your grandma/grandpa!’” Dorn stated. “A helpful thing to do instead is keep the mood light and say something like, ‘OK! I love you so much and can’t wait to hear all about what you’ve been up to.’”.

It’s never too late to start being more mindful of how you approach interactions with your grandchildren.

You can also suggest other ways to connect like waving hello or goodbye, or giving a fist bump or a high five.

“Kids often feel like they don’t have a lot of self-determination, so it can be a powerful message to send that important grown-ups in their life will respect their body boundaries no matter what,” Dorn stated. “This approach also reinforces the idea that physical affection is a personal choice, promoting a healthy understanding of boundaries and consent in other areas of their life.”.

Parenting styles and best practices change over time. You may have raised your children in a different way than your adult children are now raising their own kids.

According to recent reports, “Of course, grandparents grew up in a different era with different customs and norms, and it’s natural to want to comment on the differences,” Howes said. “There’s nothing inherently wrong with pointing out these distinctions, but it’s very easy for those comments to come across as shaming. By shaming, I mean declaring that one way was right and another is wrong, and that there is something wrong with the grandchild or their parents.”.

According to recent reports, generally speaking, it’s best to keep those comments to yourself unless you see “significant blindspots or areas that could potentially be harmful for the child,” Howes said. “Even then, it’s best to take concerns to the parents instead of the grandchild.”.

Sharing these kinds of judgments or negative comments about your adult child’s parenting choices with your grandkids is not a good idea, he noted.

“If grandparents have a beef with how their child is parenting, they should bring it up to them or keep it to themselves, but leave the grandchildren out of it,” Howes said.

The original version of this story was published on HuffPost at an earlier date.

#228302. Sleep-Unders Are Honestly a Win for Everyone

📅 08 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (301 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Tinybeans ↗ Open Full Page

Sleep-Unders Are Honestly a Win for Everyone

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (301 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tinybeans

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As soon as kids hit school age, the pressure of the sleepover begins.
  • The sleep-under brings the best elements of the sleepover and avoids the actual sleeping-over part.
  • Recent findings suggest that all the festivities are concluded just before bedtime, when parents return to swoop up their little ones and everyone heads back home to sleep in their own beds.

As soon as kids hit school age, the pressure of the sleepover begins. Whether your little one wants to host a crew of first graders in your living room (hard pass) or is being asked to sleep over at someone else’s house, there are a lot of questions that come with the milestone. Will my kid have fun? Will they sleep at all? Will they be overwhelmed? Add to that concerns surrounding safety, and it’s a tough position for parents to be in. The solution: the “sleep-under.”.

The sleep-under brings the best elements of the sleepover and avoids the actual sleeping-over part. It’s become a trendy birthday party theme because it puts less pressure on kids and the parents hosting. How it works is that kids show up to the host house all ready for a sleepover, usually around dinner time. Guests might even arrive decked out in their coziest PJs to add to the whole sleepover vibe. The group enjoys pizza, watches a movie, plays some games, and does an activity like decorating cupcakes.

Recent findings suggest that all the festivities are concluded just before bedtime, when parents return to swoop up their little ones and everyone heads back home to sleep in their own beds. Nobody is over-tired the next day. Nobody needs to call home for a late-night pickup when they have a nightmare. No parent has to stress over whether it’s a good idea to leave their kid overnight with someone they only know from the pick-up line. No kid has to feel ashamed if they aren’t yet ready to sleep away from their parents for the night. The sleep-under side-steps all those potential complications.

Sources indicate that honestly, it’s pretty genius. We just wish it were a thing when we were kids!

#228300. 21 Easy Play Ideas for Kids (Whether You Have 5, 15, or 30 Minutes)

📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1639 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tinybeans ↗ Open Full Page

21 Easy Play Ideas for Kids (Whether You Have 5, 15, or 30 Minutes)

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1639 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tinybeans

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Between daily parenting duties, work, and navigating the current world in general, saying your days are full is probably an understatement.
  • According to recent reports, even five minutes can make a difference in a child’s emotional well-being.
  • The good news is, there are lots of ways to play that take next-to-no prep.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Between daily parenting duties, work, and navigating the current world in general, saying your days are full is probably an understatement. And while your kid’s day may be full of exploration and creativity, they can also experience a lot of anxiety, stress, and pressure. That makes it even more important to have some positive, uninterrupted time to reconnect.

According to recent reports, even five minutes can make a difference in a child’s emotional well-being. But as Randy McCoy, VP of Product & Curriculum for The Little Gym, reminds us, how long you play is less vital than how often. “It’s not necessarily the ‘duration of play’ but the ‘frequency of play’ that matters most,” Mccoy notes. “If a parent can give their child their undivided attention and play with them just five minutes a day, every day, they’re on the right track.”.

The good news is, there are lots of ways to play that take next-to-no prep. Read on for 21 easy ideas to play with your kids, whether you have five minutes, 15, or more.

When you have a few minutes, whether it’s before school or after dinner, bust out these little-to-no-prep basics you can use just about anywhere.

Industry observers note that 1. Try out “Would You Rather?” kid edition. Spend a fun five minutes taking turns asking questions like, “Would you rather never eat ice cream again or get a trampoline?” or “Ride a dinosaur for 20 miles or an elephant for an hour?” The sillier the better. This also makes a great road trip game.

2. Make a dictionary dash. Grab a dictionary and choose a word at random. Read it out loud and have the kids guess what it means. If they can read, they can take turns finding words and trying to stump you.

Industry observers note that 3. Tickle your sidekick’s funny bone. Whip out brain busters or riddles that will make them laugh. Luckily, you don’t need Comedy Central writers for this one. We think your goofballs will get a kick out of our ultimate list of jokes for kids.

4. A few rounds of “We’re going on a picnic” alphabet-style will entertain the tot lot. The first player up says, “I’m going on a picnic,” then adds a tasty packable to the phrase, like an apple, apricot, or avocado. Stick with ABC order or focus on just one letter for each round.

In a recent development, 5. Play 20 questions. Have your kids guess what you’re thinking of, and keep it simple, like something you can see from where you’re standing.

6. Play a classic game of Rock, Paper, Scissors—Japanese style. It’s called Janken. Start by saying “saisho wa guu.” Then “janken pon” as you pump, before throwing on “pon.” The winning combos are still the same in this timeless, quick game you can play at home or on the go.

Sources indicate that 7. Turn yourself into a living “spot the difference” puzzle. Start with a slow model turn, then disappear and make a quick change out of sight. When you come back, your cutie’s got to spot what’s different. Did you take off a cap? Put on a scarf? Untie a shoe? Keep it easy for the tots, and kick it up a notch for older kiddos (only one earring!). Then let them have a turn trying to stump you.

8. Try out a sequencing game when the wanderlust takes hold. Name a person, place, and object, all starting with the same letter of the alphabet, then string them together like kids lining up for the school bus. “Alice from Australia loves alligators!” See how far you can get in a short amount of time.

In a recent development, for parents, playing with our kids allows us to step out of all those daily parental duties and, as McCoy explains, build friendship between parent and child. “It provides an opportunity for you to interact with them on a different level,” he says. “For a special moment, you step out of the ‘parent’ role and step into a playmate role.”  Take a break from your to-do list and try one of these 15-minute ideas that will thrill the kids and relax you, too.

It has been revealed that 9. Post-It style. A stack of Post-It notes and a pen are all it takes to play this short-and-sweet variation of the classic guessing game for parties. Choose someone to be “it.” Write on the Post-It note the name of a character from a book, movie, or show that your kid will recognize—it can be a famous person, someone they know, or a fictional character. Stick the note to their forehead, without letting them see what you wrote. Now take turns going around the room giving “it” clues to help them guess who is on their head.

10. Curl up with a good book. Putting out a basket of books in a central location motivates the kids to take a look through the pages when they’ve got time to spare. Add in a sweet bookmark that keeps track of time to make it count.

Industry observers note that 11. Give them their daily feels. Keep your favorite sensory bin fillers on hand (like cotton balls and dry beans), along with trinkets to bury and cups for spilling and filling. When you’ve got a short window, pull out the bin, fill ‘er up, and watch your kids dig and drizzle until it’s time to go.

12. Set up a quick cotton ball and straw race. Perfect for the kitchen table before lunch is served. Have siblings challenge each other for the pole position on a straightaway down the center of the table, or set up a simple obstacle course using cups that the kiddos have to work around. Ready, set, go!

Sources indicate that 13. Give a penny for their thoughts when they write in a journal. Setting aside a short amount of time to write (each day!) is a great way to encourage your amateur author’s creativity. Use silly or thought-provoking prompts to get them thinking, like, “The first time I tried …” or “When I get to be principal, I’ll …” or even “The craziest thing that happened today…” Write on, brother!

14. Give up the charade. Have your little monkey stay in character when you play a quick game of animal charades. No prep is necessary for this easy guessing game. Just pick your favorite animal and go for it! With each successful guess, trade places and start again. Ee-i-ee-i-o!

Whether your aim is active playtime or quiet(er) crafting time, filling a cool 30 minutes with your kids is easier than you think. It may take a bit of planning, but once the prep is done, it’s a sit-back-and-relax situation that’s well worth the time upfront.

15. All things LEGO. If LEGO was the first thing that popped into your head, then we’re right there with you. They’re the forever fallback for a reason, but to hit that half-hour sweet spot, try throwing a LEGO challenge into the mix: building a car that can also work underwater, or constructing a tower that’s at least 24 inches tall. Then let your master-builder go to work.

Industry observers note that 16. Spin them right round. Ana at Babble Dabble Do has a upcoming way to play with Perler beads. She puts them to work teaching science and playing tricks when these melted beauties become spinning tops. It’s just the right amount of make-and-play to fill a brief window in your busy day.

In a recent development, 17. One for the movers and shakers. Print out (and laminate if you’re feeling bold) The Alerting Activity Game, designed by Training Happy Hearts. Keep the deck on hand to stack the odds in your favor when the kids need something to do. With simple activities like “jump up and down ten times” or “pretend to be a volcano,” it’s packed with energy-burning activities that kids can run through on their own or with you!

In a recent development, 18. Bring the outside in and paint it. If snow isn’t covering your yard, go for a hunt for leaves, evergreen boughs, and sticks. Then take your findings to the craft table to fancy them up with paint. Acrylics work great for this project.

For activities that span the hour, the two-step Make & Play approach works well. You may want to do a little prep the day before to make it easier, like putting crafting necessities into one small bin that you can pull out to surprise the kids.

Recent findings suggest that 19. Wage war. Ah, the classic card game that is so simple to learn and so hard to win. It is possible that a game of war can take longer than one hour, but it rarely takes less. You do two card battles with the highest card the winner until one person has all the cards. Get the complete rules here.

According to recent reports, 20. Create a mini catapult. Little Bins for Little Hands has an awesome tutorial, using craft sticks and other office supplies you’re sure to have around the house. Once it’s built, set up target practice plates before letting the marshmallows fly.

21. Put on a show. Puppets never get old; they’re easy to make with an old sock, brown paper lunch bag, or even familiar characters glued to craft sticks. Whatever method you choose, spend time creating and playing with puppets when you’ve got an hour or more to spare. Be sure to stock the craft bin with all kinds of googly eyes, buttons, yarn, and doo-dads to help bring your buddies to life. Then find an old sheet or use a baby’s blanket draped over the table to create a stage. Bravo!

It’s that time again. Yup, your Elf on the Shelf is about to parachute in to make your life (slightly) more challenging for the next few weeks. Get ahead of the game and prep your bag of tricks with these brilliant ideas. From Elf on the Shelf clothes to last-minute Elf on the Shelf ideas that’ll make the whole family giggle, we’ve got enough easy Elf ideas to last you the entire holiday season.

Industry observers note that I remember when my kids were little, and they got their first elves. Not going to lie, remembering to move the thing every night was a struggle. But when I made the effort and managed to pull off even the easiest of Elf ideas, the look in their eyes was priceless.

It has been revealed that 1. Elf held captive. If you have two Scout elves, this easy Elf idea is a lot of fun. Pull out a toy train and a string, and decide which elf is going to be extra naughty by tying up the other one.

Industry observers note that 2. Plan a hot cocoa party. This is fun on the first night or maybe on a weekend day. Get mugs, instant cocoa, and marshmallows set up in advance and settle the elves against the mugs. Snag printables for the party here.

It has been revealed that 3. Spell it out. Do you have Scrabble tiles or Bananagrams? Then it’s a cinch to let your elf leave a sweet message for your littles to discover the next day.

According to recent reports, 4. Caught in the act. With this easy elf idea, you’ll use a bag of M&Ms, chocolate chips, or even a box of sugar cereal, and position your elf with its backside out of the bag.

5. Exhausted elf. All those trips up to the North Pole make for one tired elf. Let your little one in red take a day off. Make them a little bed with a doll blanket and a cotton ball for a pillow.

6. Deeds worth doing. Since reporting good deeds to Santa is your elf’s duty, it’s the perfect opportunity to remind kids about the spirit of Christmas. We dig the free downloadable from Over the Significant Moon.

7. Elf spaghetti. Whip up Buddy the Elf’s favorite dish for your little helper. Hint: this is a great idea for the night you make pasta. You’ll also need syrup (of course), marshmallows, candy, and chocolate syrup. Find out how to make a batch over at Instructables.

8. Riding the banister. Those naughty elves are always looking for an adrenaline rush! Use a Frisbee and sticky tape to get your little buddy set up at the top and ready to ride.

Industry observers note that 9. Sitting pretty. Have your elf take a seat inside your wreath or on the holiday table for a picture-perfect spot.

Recent findings suggest that 10. Play games. Set up your elf mid-move with this adorable mini-Twister printable.

11. Window view. If you’ve got a window and a curtain rod, you’ve got a sweet spot to hang your elf. Easy-peasy.

In a recent development, 12. Rock climbing wall. All you need is several pre-made bows to make a route for your elf.

13. Coloring elf. Take 30 seconds to scribble in a coloring book or on a printable, scatter crayons, and set up your elf. Giggles are guaranteed!

15. Zipline. This Elf on the Shelf idea is popular, but it does take a little time to set up. All you need is string or yarn, a candy cane, and a way to secure your elf to the candy cane!

It has been revealed that 16. LEGO throne. Whether you use DUPLO or LEGO, making a seat for Santa’s little helper can be done in less than five minutes.

Sources indicate that 17. Elf in the kitchen. Got a play kitchen? Then let your elf whip up something yummy.

18. On the road. With a toy car, your elf can go just about anywhere they want to go. Headed to buy a Christmas tree? Done. Want to take Wonder Woman out on a date? Totally!

Sources indicate that 19. Play Picasso. A dry-erase marker, a family photo, and a sense of humor are all you need. Give your kids beards and cat ears: See how much they laugh!

20. Put the elf in the freezer. Your elf sure does miss the North Pole! Give him a little time to chill.

According to recent reports, 21. Toilet paper tricks. Add an elf to a roll of toilet paper and send them down the stairs. Don’t have a second level? Leave a trail of written messages down the hall instead.

22. Bath time. You don’t need a Barbie bath to let your Elf soak aching bones— a plastic bowl or storage container will do the trick. Add marshmallows for bubbles, and you’re set.

23. Gone fishing. Your kids will love waking up to find the elf “fishing” for goldfish crackers in the bathroom sink.

24. Story time. Position the elf with a favorite holiday book and a captivated audience.

25. Hanging by a limb. Any elf will feel right at home when dangling from a branch of the Christmas tree.

26. Spa day. Wrap your elf in a paper towel, give them cucumber eye patches, and just like that, it’s a spa day.

27. Puzzle play. Settling your elf in for the night with a puzzle is easy and fun.

28. Paper bag race. Take those lunch bags that have been cluttering your drawer and collect a few stuffies. Then, stage a sack race-style scene across your dining room table or kitchen island.

According to recent reports, 29. Elfie selfie. Position your elf in front of the family laptop and snap a picture. Just be forewarned, if it’s a laptop you use, you’ll need to get it set back up before the kids get home from school.

Industry observers note that 30. Sweet snow angels. It’s not quite as cold down here as it is at the North Pole. When your elf gets antsy for chilly weather, make them a personal snow angel. You can use flour (but it’s messy), sprinkles, or rice, which is my personal favorite because it’s the easiest to clean up!

31. All wrapped up. Give your elf the scissors, tape, and wrapping paper. Scatter shredded paper and tape around, and it’ll be like they were caught in the act of wrapping up Santa’s gifts!

Sources indicate that 32. Elf making popcorn. Someone’s ready for family movie night!

Recent findings suggest that 33. Don’t move the elf. Well, it looks like your kids were so well-behaved that no North Pole reporting was needed. It’s also the perfect excuse for one of those nights you forget to move them.

34. Cards, anyone? Didn’t you know elves love to play games? They do, and they love to be caught mid-game.

35. A Stuck Elf. This is a super-easy elf idea, and you don’t even need the message board to pull it off. Just grab a mason jar or an empty water bottle and a prominent place to display your elf’s tight situation.

Recent findings suggest that 36. S’more to love. Some toothpicks, roasted marshmallows, chocolate squares, graham crackers, and tea lights are all you need to set up this cozy and easy elf idea.

According to recent reports, 37. Read all about it. Prop them up on a favorite Christmas story or beloved book.

Recent findings suggest that 38. Caught red-handed. Have your elf stage a scene of questionable actions and tape up the area with crepe paper.

Industry observers note that 39. Photo editor. They can’t help but make mischief, and marking up a festive photo is a silly way to say, “Elf wuz here.”.

40. Riding dinos. If you’ve got a plastic dinosaur (T. rex preferred), then you’ve got what you need to give your elf a prehistoric ride.

It has been revealed that 41. Send the Elf back to the North Pole. Possibly one of our favorite easy elf ideas: on Christmas Morning, make sure they’re out of sight, and of course, leave a note.

How Fatherhood Changes Men's Brains And Bodies Forever

📅 30 May 2025 | ⏱️ 2 min read (438 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Fatherly

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Men experience neurobiological and physiological changes to prime them for fatherhood — not unlike how women’s bodies prepare them for motherhood.
  • In a recent development, we know how women’s bodies adapt to motherhood.
  • In a recent development, in 2014, a team of scientists at Emory University recruited 88 heterosexual, biological, married fathers of children between the ages of 1 and 2, for an unprecedented experiment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Men experience neurobiological and physiological changes to prime them for fatherhood — not unlike how women’s bodies prepare them for motherhood.

In a recent development, we know how women’s bodies adapt to motherhood. Hormonal shifts, neurological flips, and, of course, the obvious post-partum biological changes. But only recently have scientists begun to focus on how men’s bodies adapt to fatherhood. We now know that fathers experience changes in their hormone levels (especially testosterone and oxytocin); their brains respond differently to parent-related stimuli, and even their socioeconomic status tends to change once children arrive.

Here’s the data behind these conclusions:.

In a recent development, in 2014, a team of scientists at Emory University recruited 88 heterosexual, biological, married fathers of children between the ages of 1 and 2, for an unprecedented experiment. They tested their hormone levels (among other metrics) and compared these results to a group of 50 non-fathers. One of the most striking results is depicted below. Compared to non-fathers, dads had lower levels of testosterone, a male hormone linked to aggression, and higher levels of oxytocin, a hormone thought to play a role in maternal (and now, perhaps, paternal) attachment. The findings suggest that fathers, not just mothers, experience hormonal changes to help them adapt to their fresh roles as highly attached and less aggressive caregivers.

After running the hormone analysis, the researchers at Emory took the experiment one step further. They hooked each man up to an fMRI—which measures activation of different brain regions—and show him images of children and adults making happy, sad, and neutral faces. In the middle frontal gyrus, a brain region responsible for face emotion processing, fathers’ brain activities spiked for children’s faces significantly more than for adult faces. As depicted below, non-father brains made no such distinction. The results suggest that fathers’ brains change, too, helping them augment empathy towards children.

Beyond the biological implications of fatherhood, studies have shown that men with children experience psychological and social changes, too. But, unlike women who take pay cuts when they give birth, the financial impact of fatherhood on men is quite positive. The data below comes from City University of New York research, which found that fathers in the city have made more money, on average, than non-fathers since at least 1990. It is unclear whether the sudden burden of diapers and saving for college drives men to earn more, or whether it’s simply wealthier men who choose to start families. But one thing is clear from the preponderance of research: fatherhood changes men. Financially, hormonally, and neurologically.

Tech Report: What Gut Health Actually Means, In A World Where The Algorithm Is Constantly Shilling Supplements

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1121 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scarymommy

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here’s what experts actually look for, recommend, and see as red flags.
  • Recent findings suggest that nervous system regulation, sleepmaxxing, high-functioning burnout — there is always some hot fresh health topic du jour.
  • We’ve heard the term; what does it actually mean?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here’s what experts actually look for, recommend, and see as red flags.

Recent findings suggest that nervous system regulation, sleepmaxxing, high-functioning burnout — there is always some hot fresh health topic du jour. While there’s usually some kernel of true health information buried in the hype, it’s hard to parse what really matters from all the social media “gurus” shilling supplements at the link in bio. This is especially true of “gut health,” a topic that feels like it has dominated wellness spaces for the past few years but also never really comes up in your primary care doctor’s office. So, what does gut health actually mean, particularly for women? What do we need to know, and what is social media fluff?

We’ve heard the term; what does it actually mean? In general, gut health refers to the state of your gastrointestinal tract and how it’s working for you, according to the American Medical Association (AMA). Regular bowel movements, no persistent pain or bloating — these are signs things are going well. Medically speaking, good gut health doesn’t mean you’ve somehow optimized your microbiome (more on that in a minute); it means your digestive tract is functioning as it should, you’re absorbing the nutrients you need, and you’re comfortable throughout the process.

“I think that it looks different for everybody, but when I have a healthy gut, I feel better overall in my day-to-day life. It’s no bloating on a consistent basis. It’s having regular bowel movements. I’m not racing to the bathroom with loose stools or, on the other side of it, I’m not going days constipated. I don’t feel that brain fog. I have energy, and I’m sleeping well,” says Chloe Melas, NBC News correspondent and author of The Girl’s Guide to Guts, who lives with ulcerative colitis, a type of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).

Yes, it is a real thing and the subject of reams of medical research.

Inside your intestines live trillions of microorganisms that have a surprising impact on our overall health. According to The Cleveland Clinic, they help break down our food, support our immune systems, and may even play a role in mood and behavioral health. There’s no one perfect gut microbiome either, according to the AMA. Each person’s is unique and depends on their age, diet, medications, genetics, where they live, and more.

It’s normal to have an off tummy day every now and then, sure, but from her own experience and speaking with experts while writing her book, Melas knows there are certain red flags women should watch for when it comes to their gut health.

“If you’re having blood in your stool on a consistent basis, and that more than a handful of times, you need to go see a doctor immediately. That can look like going to see your primary care. Personally, in my experiences in writing this book and interviewing so many different experts, and just what I've gone through in my own life having IBD, I’d say go straight to a gastroenterologist,” Melas says.

According to recent reports, vomiting, unexplained weight loss, chronic stomach pain, and difficulty swallowing are also red flags, per the AMA. Inconsistent bowel movements, whether that means racing to the bathroom multiple times a day or being chronically constipated, are another reason to schedule an appointment with your doctor, she adds. Cramping, painful bloating, or looking pregnant after eating a meal — these things are not normal, says Melas.

Industry observers note that ignoring early signs of GI challenges can keep you from feeling your best, and in some cases, missing a diagnosis you need. Women are twice as likely as men to have IBS, according to the American College of Gastroenterology.

In a recent development, “For so long, so many of us have just sort of been like, ‘This is just the way life is.’ I think that as women, we just don’t prioritize our health like we should, especially when it comes to our gut health. We’re really good about getting our mammograms and talking about our breast health. We are now finally talking about perimenopause and those symptoms. But 45 million Americans suffer from IBS. Nearly 4 million Americans suffer from inflammatory bowel disease, which raises your chances of having colon cancer. And these are things that require a doctor to help you diagnose.”.

According to recent reports, probiotic sodas, gummies, powders... what do experts say will actually help improve your GI health and comfort? What will actually make your microbiome happy, and what’s not worth the money? Health experts agree that a diet rich in fiber is the best way to support your gut’s health.

According to recent reports, “I had the privilege of interviewing Dr. William Lee, and he wrote a famous book called Eat to Beat Disease. He remarked that you have 39 trillion different bacteria that live inside your microbiome and that you need this gut diversity to have overall good health, and that it really just comes down to having a diverse plate every day when you’re sitting down for your meals,” Melas says.

It’s generally recommended for adults to consume 25 to 30 grams of fiber per day, which Melas admits can be hard sometimes with diet alone. That may mean a fiber supplement is worth the investment for you, or it may mean snacking on more fruits and veggies throughout the day where you can.

“We all get so overwhelmed; we’re constantly being targeted by drink this, eat that, take this supplement, take these vitamins. But Dr. Lee notes that really what you need is in the front of the grocery store. It's the fruits, it's the vegetables, and that it's the things that are easiest to reach first,” Melas adds.

Ultimately, Melas claims she wants more women to prioritize their health, and not to be embarrassed or afraid to talk to their providers about GI health specifically.

“If you are not having regular bowel movements, and by that I mean a major, beautiful, healthy poop every single day, then something is off with your gut health, full stop, and you need to get it figured out,” she indicates. “If you are bloated all the time, if you feel like every time you eat that cheese or a certain meal that you all of a sudden look like you’re three months pregnant, you’re not imagining it and you’re not crazy. We’ve just been told for so long to normalize it, and it's embarrassing, and it's not sexy, and who wants to sit around with your girlfriends at night and talk about the consistency of your stools? But we need to be talking about it because, honestly, it could save lives.”.

What They Don’t Tell You About Paternity Leave

📅 09 Jun 2025 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1261 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fatherly

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Paternity leave is a time to take in the necessary seismic shift in the way you think about time management, work, and life.
  • The first month that you have a child is life-changing in ways that are hard to describe.
  • Industry observers note that don’t become a statistic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paternity leave is a time to take in the necessary seismic shift in the way you think about time management, work, and life.

The first month that you have a child is life-changing in ways that are hard to describe. While there is plenty of scientific research to back up the idea that fathers get their brains rewired by having a child, the biggest change that occurs is that your concept of time is forever altered. And that’s why, at the start of your child’s life, you need to take some time off. Taking paternity leave is one of the most important things a dad can do, not just for their partner and their child, but for themselves. This may seem obvious on paper, but the vast majority of men who have access to reasonable paternity leave benefits end up not taking advantage of it.

Industry observers note that don’t become a statistic. Your time will become more precious to you than ever before once you’re a parent. And paternity leave is the only buffer you have to get yourself and your family adjusted to the new normal.

Here’s how dads need to advocate for paternity leave, and what to do with your time once it happens.

It has been revealed that regardless of the job you're in or the pay structure, the conversation with your boss about leave shouldn’t be a question of permission, it should be a conversation about how much time you’re taking off. There may be some legal questions about what your state is technically obligated to offer you, so certainly do your homework first. But, even in the absence of a clear paternity leave policy, you shouldn’t be begging for time, but rather, approaching the conversation as a negotiation for exactly how much time is reasonable for you, versus what makes sense for your job.

If your job already has a paternity leave policy, the amount of time you should take should be the maximum amount offered. “But I don’t need all that time?” you say. Well, you probably do.

Sources indicate that you’re going to end up needing other parenting time off, and you’re going to have to negotiate a upcoming relationship with work. This is one of the many things that paternity leave does. From pretty much now until the end of time you will have someone else’s schedule on your mind. This will impact your work schedule — not for better or worse, it just will — and paternity leave is your transition to this new juggling of schedules. In another sense, you’re setting a precedent with your job. Do you want it to be one that is sustainable? If so, take paternity leave.

No matter how you think of your career, having a kid is, without question, a pivot point for it. Before now, work-life balance was more of a theory; a calculus about how many drinks you could have at happy hour versus how hungover you’d be the next day. Having a child makes all of those prior considerations seem quaint. And so, the best way to think about paternity leave is that it’s the transition from one kind of career to the next.

In your previous life, you managed your time and money, perhaps, with a shoulder shrug and a “good enough” mentality. But being a parent isn’t like that. Everything you do, from hitting a deadline to taking out the trash, matters a little bit more. Good enough isn’t really good anymore. Yes, you’re going to make mistakes. That’s what parenting is all about. But it’s also nothing like a job. You’re not clocking in and out. If you think you’re suddenly going to have time off from being a parent, you won’t.

According to recent reports, this is what makes time management so crucial — and why you need to take paternity leave to get your upcoming schedule in order. Because you’re not at work, you are able to live in this period of transition. It’s weird. It’s hard. But without paternity leave, you’d barely be able to process it.

Unless you are the primary caregiver who is nursing with the child, the vast majority of the time you’ll have a job that will suddenly be more important than you’ve ever realized — cleaning up. When it comes to bottles, breast pump parts, fresh baby clothes, and blankets, keeping everything clean in those early months is essential. If your wife was the person who did laundry before, or kept an eye on your dirty dishes, those days are over.

Here’s a hot tip: Do you still have your apron from when you waited tables? Don’t have an apron? Get an apron. Preferably one with pockets. It's great for storing bottles, burp clothes, diapers, and pretty much everything else to keep your household sane.

Recent findings suggest that when you add it all up, parents lose about six years of sleep when they have a child. This will not magically get resolved when your child turns six, by the way. But the strange sleep patterns that you have during those first few weeks are truly hellish. The only way to deal with this is to accept it as soon as possible. Again, this is one of the reasons why paternity leave is so key. Both you and your partner are going to have to come up with an ad hoc sleep schedule in order to literally not lose your minds.

It has been revealed that the sooner you understand that feeding and caring for a newborn is like working a double shift that never ends, the better. If you slept on a few chairs pushed together in the delivery room when your kid was born, the first month or two aren’t too different from that. It does get better, but the sooner you get over how horrible it is, the better.

It has been revealed that chances are, your partner will be even more exhausted than you are. And so, amid all the cleaning, helping, and wrestling in your mind with your raging id, you have to remember how special this time is. Yes, take a ton of pictures. No, you’ll never regret taking a million pictures when your child is a newborn. If anything, these photos will become even more incredible to you as the years pass. You’re lucky to live in a time when you have a movie studio in your pocket. Take advantage of it. Pay for the extra phone data. Get those digital photos printed up into albums right away. It’s all worth it.

Sources indicate that but when you’re not being the support parent, when you’re not contemplating how the rest of your life is forever different, the best thing you can do is hold your child as much as possible. You’ve probably heard of the “football” grip by now, the thing where you can fit your kid into the crook of your arm. This is one of the coolest things ever, and it may seem like it will never end, but you won’t believe how fast this time goes.

Sources indicate that newborn babies sleep all the time. Yes, statistically, they’re going to do a major chunk of that sleeping with mom. But you’re on paternity leave for one big reason, a reason that is more notable than all the other reasons: You need to put that kind on your chest, and in your arms, and make sure this little person knows that they are safe with you, forever.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We can already feel the tension spreading through our bodies: It’s time to put away the iPad, but there is a small person who is almost certainly going to lose their mind when you tell them. Whether you resort to a countdown timer or go the “this is your last show” route, it’s pretty much always a struggle.

Industry observers note that perhaps you need a new strategy. Parenting coach Dr. Chelsey Hauge-Zavaleta recently shared her method for successfully ending iPad time, and it combines a little bit of the two approaches above with some voice modulation and sensory input.

Industry observers note that A few things to note about this method. Using language like “We have one more song” instead of “This is our last song before we leave for school” focuses on what the child is doing now versus what you are doing in the future. It’s easier for kids to accept the transition this way.

Industry observers note that “Melodic intonation” is when you use a sing-songy voice to make a statement. It helps kids notice what you are saying and acknowledge it. Take a look at Miss Rachel and a lot of the other preschool-focused programming, and you’ll see it employed often. Using melodic intonation for the phrase “iPad is all done” helps to signal the transition for the child.

It’s notable to remember that even when using a technique like this, it will take you doing it the same way over and over several times before your child catches on and gets with the program. If they have a meltdown, don’t engage; stay calm; and move on.
